item.title: China-Africa economic, trade expo opens South Africa session
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
China-Africa economic, trade expo opens South Africa session A man visits the fifth South Africa International Industrial Expo in Johannesburg, South Africa, Nov. 19, 2026. The South Africa session of the China-Africa Economic and Trade Expo kicked off in Johannesburg on Thursday, with South African officials and business representatives calling for deeper trade and investment ties with China. Held alongside the fifth South Africa International Industrial Expo, the three-day event provides a platform for businesses from the two countries to explore opportunities, establish partnerships and secure business deals. (Xinhua/Chen Wei) JOHANNESBURG, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- The South Africa session of the China-Africa Economic and Trade Expo kicked off in Johannesburg on Thursday, with South African officials and business representatives calling for deeper trade and investment ties with China. Held alongside the fifth South Africa International Industrial Expo (SAIIE), the three-day event provides a platform for businesses from the two countries to explore opportunities, establish partnerships and secure business deals. Speaking at the opening ceremony, John Steenhuisen, South Africa's deputy minister of trade, industry and competition, said the two countries shared a vision of building a partnership based on deeper economic cooperation and mutual development. He urged businesses from both sides to make full use of the expo to explore opportunities. A total of 40 South African companies and more than 190 Chinese manufacturers are exhibiting at the SAIIE. The exhibition covers 5,000 square meters and features four sections, namely power and energy, machinery and parts, mining, and African products. China extended zero-tariff treatment to all 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic relations on May 1. Chinese Ambassador to South Africa Wu Peng said the bilateral trade had grown notably since the policy took effect, adding that Chinese companies were keen to invest in South Africa and contribute to its economic development and job creation. Simohn Engelbrecht, head of trade and relations at Agriculture South Africa, said South Africa was well positioned to supply China with a variety of agricultural products throughout the year and was seeking to diversify its exports to the Chinese market. "Ultimately, the opportunity for us is not only to increase trade volumes, but also to build a stronger and more diversified economic relationship between South Africa and China," Engelbrecht said. A series of business matchmaking sessions focusing on agricultural machinery, new energy and watches will also be held during the three-day event to facilitate business partnerships and trade deals between Chinese and South African companies. item.title: Xi says China ready for closer cooperation with Malaysia
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
Xi says China ready for closer cooperation with Malaysia Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 20, 2026. Anwar is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- China stands ready to foster greater momentum for cooperation with Malaysia to bring more benefits to people of both countries, President Xi Jinping said Friday. China-Malaysia relations have maintained high-level development since the two sides reached important consensus on building a high-level strategic China-Malaysia community with a shared future and ushered in a new "Golden 50 Years" for bilateral ties in April last year, he said. Xi made the remarks when meeting with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. China and Malaysia should maintain high-level strategic communication and support each other in safeguarding their respective national sovereignty, security and development interests, Xi said at the meeting. The two sides should also ensure high-quality development and operation of key projects, expand and improve agricultural product trade, and broaden cooperation in tourism, education and other areas, he added. Xi called for joint efforts to advance the reform of global governance, strengthen coordination and cooperation within multilateral frameworks such as APEC, and safeguard the common interests of developing countries. Anwar said the Taiwan question is China's internal affair, and Malaysia firmly adheres to the one-China policy. He said Malaysia is ready to strengthen strategic coordination with China, give full play to the role of bilateral cooperation mechanisms, ensure the sound operation of key infrastructure projects, and enhance cooperation in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence. Malaysia will also promote inter-civilization exchanges and dialogue, step up coordination and collaboration in international affairs, and keep elevating the level of Malaysia-China relations, Anwar said. Anwar attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting held from Wednesday to Thursday in Shenzhen. item.title: Xi says China, Australia should be mutually trusted partners
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
Xi says China, Australia should be mutually trusted partners SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Friday that China and Australia should be cooperative partners who trust each other and help each other succeed, as the two countries have no historical grievances or fundamental conflicts of interests. China-Australia relations are stable at present, said Xi when meeting with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Xi said that in a volatile and turbulent world, the two countries should enhance mutual trust, accommodate each other's core interests and major concerns, and keep to the right direction of friendship and cooperation. He called for deepening mutually beneficial cooperation in pursuit of the two countries' respective development goals, advancing traditional cooperation in agriculture, energy and minerals, and expanding cooperation in emerging areas such as the green economy, new energy, the digital industry, artificial intelligence and climate change response. Efforts should be made to promote friendship between the two countries through expanded people-to-people exchanges, Xi said, noting that the two sides had agreed to designate 2027 as the China-Australia Year of Tourism. He also emphasized the need to strengthen multilateral coordination in addressing global challenges, advance the building of an Asia-Pacific community, and jointly uphold the international system with the United Nations at its core and the international order based on international law. item.title: Xi calls for promoting building of a China-Thailand community with a shared future to higher level
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
Xi calls for promoting building of a China-Thailand community with a shared future to higher level Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 20, 2026. Anutin is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday called for promoting the building of a China-Thailand community with a shared future to a higher level. China and Thailand should continuously enhance political mutual trust and strengthen solidarity and coordination, Xi said when meeting with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. The two countries should step up exchanges between governments, political parties, legislatures and at other levels, and safeguard their common strategic interests, Xi stressed. He called on the two sides to make good use of cooperation mechanisms in economy and trade, science and technology, and the digital economy, expand and strengthen traditional cooperation in agriculture and connectivity, and cultivate and strengthen new growth areas of cooperation such as artificial intelligence, new energy vehicles, aviation and aerospace, disaster prevention, mitigation and relief, and water resources management. The two sides should strengthen cooperation in culture, education, and tourism, Xi added. He also urged intensifying efforts to crack down on illegal and criminal activities such as online gambling and telecom fraud. The two sides should strengthen multilateral coordination and work together to safeguard the common interests of the Global South, Xi said. China is ready to play a positive role in bringing about an early turnaround in Thailand-Cambodia relations, Xi said. For his part, Anutin said Thailand is ready to continue to strengthen high-level exchanges with China and enhance cooperation in areas such as trade, investment, science and technology, industrial and supply chains, and connectivity. Thailand will resolutely crack down on cross-border crimes including online gambling and telecom fraud, and protect the safety of Chinese citizens in Thailand, he said, adding that the country welcomes more Chinese visitors. Anutin attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, held from Wednesday to Thursday. item.title: Xi says China, Singapore should strengthen strategic communication, enhance coordination
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
Xi says China, Singapore should strengthen strategic communication, enhance coordination Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 20, 2026. Wong is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Friday that China and Singapore should strengthen strategic communication and enhance solidarity and coordination as the world is undergoing accelerated changes unseen in a century. The two countries should be sincere friends who trust each other and support each other in pursuing development paths suited to their respective national conditions, said Xi when meeting with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Wong attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting held from Wednesday to Thursday in Shenzhen. During the meeting, Xi called for advancing the all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership between China and Singapore to new heights, and stressed the need for both sides to advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation. The two countries should launch negotiations for upgraded Version 4.0 of their free trade agreement, and deliver signature cooperation outcomes in areas such as the digital economy, green development, and artificial intelligence, Xi added. Noting that both countries should be "a progressive force" for championing international fairness and justice, Xi called for safeguarding regional peace and stability while jointly building an Asia-Pacific community and a community with a shared future for humanity. For his part, Wong stated that Singapore firmly adheres to the one-China policy and opposes "Taiwan independence." Singapore stands ready to work with China to enhance political mutual trust, deepen cooperation in areas such as trade, industrial and supply chains, and artificial intelligence, and promote people-to-people exchanges, the prime minister noted. Wong said Singapore is willing to strengthen communication and cooperation with the Chinese side on international affairs to jointly address global challenges. item.title: "Where there is trade, there is mutual benefit" -- perspectives from APEC CEO Summit
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
"Where there is trade, there is mutual benefit" -- perspectives from APEC CEO Summit The opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 is held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- "Where there is trade, there is mutual benefit." For renowned U.S. economist Jeffrey Sachs, the idea is simple and clearcut: the global economy need not be a zero-sum game. After attending the 2026 APEC CEO Summit, he made the point with evident enthusiasm: "It's not that we have to choose who wins and who loses. Everybody can win through peaceful cooperation." With the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," this year's APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen, a southern Chinese metropolis, brought together more than 2,000 representatives from 21 APEC economies and 13 non-APEC economies, including Britain, France, Germany and Switzerland. In interviews with Xinhua on site, several attendees shared their perspectives on free trade, innovation and cooperation, offering insights into how business leaders view the region's evolving economic landscape and the opportunities it presents. INNOVATION COOPERATION Sachs recounted his journey from Italy to China riding BYD electric vehicles, covering 15,000 km along a route inspired by Marco Polo's journey 750 years ago. "He went by horse, I went by 800 horsepower. This is the breakthrough," he said. Amid rapid technological advances, the economist noted, the prevailing sentiment is one of cooperation, with participants eager to expand trade, attract investment, pursue joint ventures and become part of the Asia-Pacific's growing economic dynamism. This view is echoed by Jacob Cooke, CEO of WPIC, a Canadian e-commerce and technology consultancy that helps global brands grow their businesses in China, Japan, South Korea and Southeast Asia. A frequent traveler to China, Cooke has witnessed firsthand the remarkable pace of innovation in cities such as Shenzhen, Shanghai, Nanjing and Hangzhou. "It's incredible," he said. He pointed to China's approach to artificial intelligence (AI), particularly its open-source and open-weight models and affordable AI solutions, which are increasingly accessible to businesses around the world. At a time when countries across the globe are looking to harness AI for their own development, he said, Chinese companies have focused on making the technology widely available rather than maximizing profits or putting up barriers to access. Seeing Chinese companies embrace this spirit of openness and sharing, much like the people of China, gives him "real optimism," he added. Rosario Navarro, president of Chile's non-profit business federation Sofofa, said Chilean companies were keen to forge partnerships with Chinese enterprises in high-tech fields, including AI. "If we engage Chinese companies with the technology that allows us to be more productive, we can clearly take a leap, and that's what we're waiting for," Navarro added. This photo taken on Nov. 19, 2026 shows the International Communication Center of Shenzhen, the venue of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Xing Guangli) OPPORTUNITIES IN CHINESE MARKET For many participants, opportunities for cooperation extend beyond technology to include talent development, industrial upgrading and other sectors. Anindya Novyan Bakrie, chairman of the Indonesian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, identified two closely related competitive advantages of the Chinese market: technology and talent. Beyond trade and business cooperation, he said, Indonesia hopes to explore ways to develop its talent pool through closer collaboration between universities and businesses in the two countries. Technology cooperation, he added, should extend beyond digital technologies and AI to include processing technologies across a wide range of industries, from critical minerals and agricultural products to traditional energy. Agricultural trade is another area where participants see scope for deeper engagement. Carlos Salinas, executive director of East Asia at the U.S. Soybean Export Council, said China remains a vital market for U.S. soybeans, while other American agricultural sectors are also keen to expand their presence in the Chinese market. Salinas said the council took part in the China International Import Expo, which concluded in Shanghai earlier this month, as part of a broader U.S. agricultural delegation. The delegation showcased not only soybeans but also a range of other American agricultural products, including grains and almonds. Scott St John, chairman of ANZ Bank New Zealand, said he had taken the opportunity to spend more time in Shenzhen and the wider region in south China's Guangdong province, visiting companies and building connections with Chinese businesses that could complement their own operations back home. The summit has sent a powerful message to the world: it is open to the world, welcomes businesses to come and explore opportunities in China, and is equally keen to reach out, promoting open and free trade for shared prosperity, he said. From New Zealand's perspective as a pro-trade nation in the Asia-Pacific, he said, "We see China as a partner that is of a similar mind." This photo taken on Nov. 18, 2026 shows an exterior view of the Qianhai International Convention Center, the venue for the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Liang Xu) OPPOSING PROTECTIONISM At the summit, participants voiced a common concern: rising protectionism and trade barriers will only make it harder to address global challenges. Against a backdrop of heightened uncertainty, economic disruptions and supply chain pressures, they stressed the need to keep markets open and strengthen economic ties. Low Kian Chuan, chairman of Malaysia-China Business Council, pointed out that with unilateralism and protectionism on the rise, we are seeing more tariffs as well as non-tariff barriers. "All these barriers add to our costs. That is why we advocate openness," he said. Martha Delgado, president of global advisory and advocacy firm APCO for Mexico and Latin America, said that at a time of mounting disputes over tariffs, trade restrictions and tighter borders, maintaining an open-minded approach was more important than ever. APEC economies should continue to strengthen their own economic capabilities while deepening regional integration, helping the Asia-Pacific consolidate its position as a major global economic powerhouse, Delgado said. Vicente Roqueni, executive president of the China Chamber of Commerce and Technology Mexico, said at a time when the world is facing so many challenges, China's efforts to promote cooperation and help countries achieve common development are particularly important. By lowering trade barriers, countries can expand commerce, promote shared prosperity and deepen collaboration, working toward a vision of a community where growth and opportunities are shared by all, he said. item.title: Xi chairs groundbreaking China-Russia-U.S. summit with Putin, Trump
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
Xi chairs groundbreaking China-Russia-U.S. summit with Putin, Trump Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday chaired a historic summit here with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump, marking the first-ever face-to-face meeting between the Chinese, Russian and U.S. heads of state. At the summit, held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, the three leaders had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security. Following the summit, the three countries released the China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, outlining their common understandings on issues including the UN reform, energy security, the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court and nuclear risk reduction. Xi described the trilateral meeting as being of groundbreaking significance. He said peace among major countries brings stability to the world, while their contention would only lead to chaos. Peace has been the enduring pursuit of humanity, Xi said, noting that the planet has experienced more than 10,000 wars and that more than 60 conflicts are still underway in various parts of the world. More than 80 years ago, China, Russia and the United States, the key anti-fascist forces in the world, fought shoulder to shoulder and achieved great victories, winning peace and tranquility for the world, he said. Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) RIGHT WAY FOR MAJOR COUNTRIES TO GET ALONG "Humanity, living in the same global village, is a community with a shared future where we all stand to benefit or lose together," Xi said. "In this global village, major countries shoulder special responsibilities. Their positive interaction is not optional, but a must." In recent years, China has been promoting the China-Russia comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination for the new era and actively developing the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, with a view to fostering major-country dynamics featuring peaceful coexistence, overall stability and balanced development to the benefit of each other and the world at large, he said. Noting that transformation not seen in a century is accelerating across the globe, Xi said the world is not peaceful and testing times reveal responsibilities on one's shoulders. As major countries and permanent members of the UN Security Council, China, Russia and the United States should set good examples, work together to meet global challenges, jointly uphold world peace and stability, and make greater contributions to the progress of humanity, Xi said. Xi made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace, calling for mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation. He said that countries should respect one another's sovereignty and territorial integrity, respect the social systems and development paths of their own choice, and respect each other's core interests and major concerns. They should not interfere in other countries' domestic affairs or each other's internal affairs, he said. "On major sensitive issues concerning one another, it is important to communicate in advance, try to see things from one another's perspective, act with caution, and in particular, not to challenge the red lines of one another," Xi said. Xi said that China, Russia and the United States should be partners and friends. "The Thucydides Trap is by no means a destiny." As the main victors of World War II, the three countries should steadfastly safeguard the postwar international order, uphold the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, and defend the hard-won outcomes of victory in World War II, Xi said. According to the trilateral declaration, the three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons. "Nuclear weapons, the Sword of Damocles that hangs over humanity, should be completely prohibited and thoroughly destroyed over time to make the world free of nuclear weapons," Xi said. He emphasized the importance of win-win cooperation. The three countries should strengthen economic cooperation and trade, and combine their respective strengths in resources, manufacturing and consumption to make the pie of cooperation bigger and achieve win-win and all-win outcomes. "Decoupling and disruption of industrial and supply chains are not the way to go," Xi said, adding that the three countries could strengthen communication and coordination to safeguard the security and stability of the global energy market. He said that the three countries should maintain regular high-level exchanges, keep dialogue channels open at all levels, and establish crisis communication and prevention mechanisms to ensure that misjudgments occur less, differences can be managed, and frictions will not escalate. "China, Russia and the United States should continue to encourage parties to a conflict to sit down and talk, and settle disputes through political and diplomatic means," he said. Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan) POSITIVE, CONSTRUCTIVE AND FRUITFUL SUMMIT Putin said that the victory in World War II brought the three countries together. Safeguarding the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and upholding international peace are their shared responsibilities, while properly addressing hotspot issues serves their common interests, he added. Russia stands ready to work with China and the United States to promote free and open international trade, safeguard energy and food security, and strengthen international cooperation on artificial intelligence governance, Putin said. Trump said that the United States, China and Russia, as nuclear powers, bear a special and important responsibility for maintaining world peace and stability. Trump said the summit is a historic event of great importance, drawing global attention. He said the three countries should jointly prevent nuclear proliferation and avert the catastrophic consequences that nuclear weapons could bring to humanity. Noting that dialogue is essential to maintaining stability and achieving peace, Trump said all issues should be resolved through dialogue. He expressed hope that the three countries better protect the planet and make the future safer. The three heads of state also exchanged views on major international and regional issues, including the Ukraine crisis, nuclear non-proliferation, the situations in the Middle East and on the Korean Peninsula. Summarizing main consensus reached at the summit, Xi described the meeting as positive, constructive and fruitful, saying that the three countries share the same view on safeguarding world peace. Xi said that the three countries remember their history of fighting side by side during World War II and stressed the need to cherish the hard-won peace. Major countries should take seriously the legitimate security concerns of all nations, he added. Dialogue and negotiation represent the right way to resolve differences, Xi said. "There is hope for peace as long as dialogue does not cease and the door does not close." He stressed that cooperation is the only way to meet challenges, calling for stronger cooperation on the basis of common interests to advance peace and pursue win-win outcomes. "The seeds sown at today's summit will surely take root, sprout, blossom and bear fruit," Xi said, calling on the three countries to follow through on the consensus reached at the summit, strengthen communication, build common ground through dialogue, promote peace via cooperation, and work together to build a better world. item.title: Xi, Prabowo announce launch of China-Indonesia comprehensive economic partnership negotiations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
Xi, Prabowo announce launch of China-Indonesia comprehensive economic partnership negotiations SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto on Friday announced the launch of negotiations for a bilateral comprehensive economic partnership. The announcement was made during Xi's meeting with Prabowo in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Prabowo is in China for the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. Xi said the two countries should strengthen strategic communication and solidarity, deepen all-round strategic cooperation, consolidate the foundation of political trust, and jointly guard against and respond to external risks. He called on both countries to expand mutually beneficial cooperation, advance major projects such as the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway, and deepen cooperation in energy and mineral resources, artificial intelligence, the digital economy, and clean energy. Xi called for efforts to reach an all-round, high-standard comprehensive economic partnership agreement at an early date. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Xi meets Trump, calling for continued efforts to steer China-U.S. relations on right course
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Xi meets Trump, calling for continued efforts to steer China-U.S. relations on right course Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with U.S. President Donald Trump, who is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan) SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping met with U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday in Shenzhen, calling for continued efforts to jointly steer the giant ship of China-U.S. relations in the right direction toward the future. Trump is in the southern Chinese city for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov. 18-19. During the meeting, Xi said that China-U.S. relations have generally maintained a stable and positive trajectory, bringing tangible benefits to people of both countries and injecting stability and certainty into the world. Xi said that he and Trump had jointly explored the right way for China and the United States, as two major countries, to get along, established a new vision to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, and given it new substance grounded in respect, fairness and reciprocity. The new vision has been welcomed by the people of both China and the United States, as well as the international community, he added. Xi stressed that building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability is an unprecedented and pioneering endeavor, adding that the key to sustaining the current positive momentum lies in taking concrete action to implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state. The two sides agreed to map out an action plan for building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability. Xi called on the two sides to strengthen communication on economic and trade matters, address each other's concerns, and work toward mutual benefit. The cooperation between the two countries on counternarcotics, repatriation of illegal immigrants, and combating telecommunications and online fraud has yielded positive results, Xi said, adding that it can be further deepened based on respect, fairness, and reciprocity. China and the United States should strengthen communication and coordination to guard against security risks of artificial intelligence (AI) and ensure that AI always remains under human control, he said. On the Taiwan question, the U.S. side should keep doing the right thing and avoid major setbacks in China-U.S. relations, Xi said. Trump said he and Xi have jointly guided the development of U.S.-China relations, adding that both leaders have maintained close contact, with their friendship growing stronger. Trade and investment ties between the two countries have continued to grow, and cooperation on fentanyl and other issues has yielded results, Trump noted. He called on both sides to maintain the positive momentum of the stable development in bilateral relations and strengthen cooperation in areas such as farm products, energy and super intelligence. The United States does not support "Taiwan independence," Trump said. He congratulated China on hosting a successful APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, adding that both countries need to work together to lead and promote world peace and stability. item.title: Xi chairs APEC meeting, calls for building Asia-Pacific community
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Xi Focus: Xi chairs APEC meeting, calls for building Asia-Pacific community Chinese President Xi Jinping chairs the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and delivers important remarks titled "Building an Asia-Pacific Community and Writing a New Chapter of the Asia-Pacific Miracle" in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu) SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for further efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community and write a new chapter of the "Asia-Pacific miracle." "We must strive to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development," Xi said as he chaired the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, on Nov. 18-19. Xi noted that for more than three decades, the Asia-Pacific region has undergone tremendous changes, creating the "Asia-Pacific miracle" of rapid economic growth. In the face of new opportunities and challenges, the region must adapt to the new realities and open up new prospects for Asia-Pacific cooperation, he added. Xi called for solidarity and mutual assistance in building an Asia-Pacific community, urging APEC economies to expand their shared interests, meet the difficulties and challenges together, and steadily foster a shared sense of community. "Members of APEC are like passengers riding the same ship. To navigate the waves of the Pacific, we must unite as one and look out for each other," he said. Xi highlighted the importance of openness and integration, calling for efforts to uphold open regionalism, steadily advance economic integration, and champion free and open trade and investment, while developing a cooperation pattern that is open and integrated rather than exclusive or fragmented. Building an Asia-Pacific community requires enterprise and innovation, Xi said, urging stronger scientific and technological cooperation, the commercialization of innovation outcomes, and an open, fair, just and nondiscriminatory environment for cooperation. He also underscored the importance of inclusive development, stressing the need to ensure that development benefits all, deliver for the people, and foster favorable conditions for turning the vision of an Asia-Pacific community into reality. FOUR PILLARS Founded in 1989, APEC now brings together 21 member economies, including China, Russia and the United States. China joined in 1991. The forum has helped expand trade and investment and strengthen economic ties across the region. "China has been an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation," Xi said at the Shenzhen meeting, adding that the country is ready to work with all parties to build the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community -- economy and trade, connectivity, innovation, and development. The Chinese president called for stronger economy and trade as a pillar underpinning such a community. Efforts should be made to align various regional economic and trade agreements, boost trade and investment facilitation and digitalization, and reduce barriers to trade and investment, he said. Xi underscored the importance of upgrading connectivity in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called for measures to improve infrastructure network, harmonize policies and regulations, advance people-to-people exchanges, and promote mutual understanding and closer bonds among peoples. Innovation should be fostered as another pillar of the Asia-Pacific community, Xi said. Greater efforts need to be made to develop digital infrastructure and encourage the broad application of artificial intelligence, he added. Xi also stressed the importance of development in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called on regional economies to advance cooperation on energy and food security, anti-corruption governance across borders, and green and low-carbon transition. He also expressed support for improving the people's well-being and called for increased investment in human capital. TURNING CONSENSUS INTO ACTION China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation, Xi said. He announced that China would contribute 20 million U.S. dollars to support APEC practical cooperation. China will also establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges, and set up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises, according to Xi. Leaders and representatives of APEC member economies shared their views at the meeting on building an Asia-Pacific community to prosper together. They spoke highly of the achievements of China's APEC host year and expressed their readiness to step up cooperation to advance APEC's development. In his closing remarks, Xi called for strengthening confidence to translate the consensus on building an Asia-Pacific community into concrete action, and to turn the vision into reality. He stressed the need to focus on development as the broadest common ground for cooperation and deliver more tangible benefits through Asia-Pacific cooperation. The meeting adopted by consensus the 2026 APEC Leaders' Declaration, which sets out the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community, and three outcome documents on trade, connectivity and innovation. Vietnam took over as APEC host for 2027, with President To Lam inviting leaders and representatives of member economies to attend next year's meeting in Vietnam.
